Definition: from a derivative of G5424; to exercise thought, i.e. be anxious:--be careful.
BiblicalUsage: Phrontizo means to be careful, to exercise thought, to be anxious to do good, and it appears once, in Paul's charge to Titus. This is a faithful saying, he writes, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that carefulness about good works is the mark of real belief: the one who has believed in God is careful to maintain the works that prove it.
